name: Can ground-up multifamily development work on a narrow lot in Burbank?

mainEntity.name: Is a narrow parcel in Burbank still viable for a new apartment project?
mainEntity.text: Is a narrow parcel in Burbank still viable for a new apartment project?

acceptedAnswer.text: A narrow parcel can absolutely be viable in Burbank, but the design must be disciplined. Narrow sites often lose efficiency because stairs, corridors, elevators, and parking consume a larger share of the building. That can reduce rent-producing area and make the project harder to finance. The key question is whether the parcel can support a functional floor plate and a parking layout that does not overtake the site. In some cases, a narrower project works better with smaller units and a simpler massing strategy. In others, the lot is simply too constrained to support the desired return. The only reliable answer comes from a feasibility study that compares several layouts before land is acquired. That study should evaluate code, parking, utility placement, and construction cost together rather than separately.
acceptedAnswer.description: A narrow lot can work if the building can still fit circulation, parking, light, and code-required setbacks. The biggest risks are inefficient floor plans and expensive parking solutions. A narrow-site feasibility study should test whether the project can still produce enough rentable area after stairs, elevators, and access are added.
